summary: Nora's ambient deciders can now see each other's verdicts. A shared decision log records every participation determination, proactive decision and tag outcome, and the participation turn and the proactive pass each read the others' rows for their whole workspace.
details: Issue #199: the proactive adaptor logged only its own reminder rows, and the determination log was written and read back into no prompt. Measured on 2026-09-10 — participation answered a question at 16:43, the tag turn one second later re-derived the whole answer and died, and the proactive decider raised the same question in another room at 18:03.

A new `decision_log` table (migration 0053), append-only, with one row per decision: which decider, which room, the verdict, a short code-derived label, the note it concerned, and when. Four writers: the fire path on every participation and proactive act determination; the proactive decide turn on every decision including its declines; and the tag path on every turn — the ones that replied, the ones that deliberately said nothing (recorded as `silent`, never `failed`: R-5's silence is the healthy outcome), and the ones that faulted.

Two readers, each excluding its own writers, both scoped to the WORKSPACE. The participation turn's prompt gains a `<loop_decisions>` block carrying what her proactive half already raised; the proactive decide turn's gains one carrying the participation and tag rows. Workspace and not room is what makes the log answer the incident at all: a proactive row fires into the workspace's home room and nowhere else, while the thread it is about runs wherever the group is talking — on 2026-09-10 those were different rooms on different platforms. The writer set goes into the QUERY, so the 24-hour / 20-row bound counts rows the reader can actually use; filtered afterwards, half an hour of one busy writer's rows fills the bound and the block renders empty in exactly the busy room where the incident happened.

Each block's note names only the deciders that block carries, and says so — a decider the reader filtered out is stated as absent rather than silently missing, so «no participation row» stops reading as «participation never ran here». It glosses every verdict it can show, says which way time runs, puts an age on every row, and contains no verb aimed at the model.

**The Relevance Gate is out of this log on both sides (DEC-179), and that holds for admission control generally, not just this gate.** Its whole shape is one call, transcript plus standing, no tools and no loop; a writer with a fail-soft path is not that, and design 36 §6 forbids it seeing what she has already raised, because a pending proactive row carries a note title. An earlier cut of this branch had the participation trigger log the gate's verdict one layer out; DEC-179 (design/ambient-loop, three reviews) held the line at BOTH sides of the seam, so that write was removed rather than kept as a lone exception. The gate's verdict remains observable only on its own metrics (`nora_relevance_gate_total` / `nora_relevance_gate_errors_total`), exactly as before this branch.

No speech, no title and no person identifier reaches a row or a render. A row carries a code-derived label — a determination's disposition, a tag turn's disposition — and never model text; the decide turn's own `why` is deliberately not stored, because it is written about a note and would carry note titles into a block whose own note says it holds no notes. A note appears as its id, which the participation turn resolves against the `<notes>` block it already has. A room appears under its operator-authored policy label or not at all.

A row is written at turn COMPLETION — after the message went out, or after the decision to stay silent was taken. That is what closes the sequential duplicate: the send at 16:43:57 is durable before the tag turn at 16:44:04 reads anything.
limitations: The tag turn WRITES but does not READ: a tag one second behind a participation answer still re-derives it. That read is a separate, smaller change (it needs a 10-minute window rather than 24 hours) and is not in this branch.

Every writer and both reads are fail-soft and bounded on a 2-second wall clock: a decision log that is down costs a thinner prompt and a counter (`nora_errors_total{stage="decision_log_read"}` / `{stage="decision_log_write"}`), never a dropped reply — so a silently degraded log reads as a quiet estate unless those series are watched.
Whether the blocks actually change either decider's verdicts is unmeasured. The proactive decide suite grades a prompt this change touches, and it has not been run against this change.

The log closes the SEQUENTIAL duplicate, not the concurrent one. A tag that lands while a participation turn is still running reads a log that does not yet contain it, and both turns answer; serialising that is `ConversationSlots`' job, and this is a record rather than a lock.

Two of the four writers — participation and tag — are read only by the proactive decide turn, which does not run where the Dreamer is off or a workspace has named no home room. In those deployments those rows are written and never read.
